overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data highlights extreme outperformance in space/planetary 'What If' scenarios and bizarre cosmic anomalies published within the last 7 days. Specifically, speculative cosmic immersion (e.g., liquid diamond planets, dark planets, burning ice) and counter-intuitive planetary physics generate significantly higher velocity, likes-per-view, and engagement than standard physiological or psychological facts. Newer 7-day cohort videos are capturing accelerated traction compared to the older September baseline.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) garnered over 1,000 views and exceptionally high likes (38+) relative to older historical baseline shorts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on sensory-driven 'What If you fell into / visited X extreme cosmic object' formats with high-contrast visual stakes.

winning_patterns.evidence: Topics focusing on extreme planetary conditions such as 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (QXuqYERlqSo) drove over 700 to 1,000+ views within days.
winning_patterns.action: Continue producing extreme planetary weather and material anomalies (e.g., helium rain, electric storms, impossible densities) utilizing striking visual hooks.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos covering memory and brain tricks such as 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A, r43-7nSn8SQ) flatlined with single-digit or low double-digit views.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract internal psychological trivia unless tied to a visceral, high-stakes external consequence or extreme visual metaphor.

weak_patterns.evidence: Titles centered around general historical mysteries or simple animal trivia without a jarring visual juxtaposition (e.g., 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever', F1kXwuXuNgo) showed weaker velocity.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid standard listicle-style animal facts; if covering animals, frame them through cinematic survival or shocking planetary-scale comparisons.
